subtitle: A teenage printer, a Pacific press, and a conspiracy carried in newsprint

panels.shot: low-angle medium close-up in a dim San Francisco printshop
panels.action: Kartar Singh Sarabha stands by a heavy hand press in a cluttered American printshop, one ink-darkened hand resting on freshly printed Ghadar sheets, eyes lifted as if already seeing across oceans.

dialogue.text: In 1913, a teenage migrant in San Francisco inked a newspaper that British judges in Lahore would later call a crime against an empire.

i18n.hi: 1913 में, सैन फ़्रांसिस्को में एक किशोर प्रवासी ने ऐसा अख़बार छापा, जिसे लाहौर के अंग्रेज़ जज बाद में सम्राज्य के ख़िलाफ़ जुर्म कहेंगे।

panels.shot: wide panoramic view of the Pacific coast dock at night
panels.action: A steamship lies at a San Francisco pier under a foggy night sky; silhouettes of Indian labourers, sailors and students move between cargo crates and looming warehouses.

dialogue.text: The story begins far from Punjab, on the cold piers of the Pacific Coast, where Indian workers and students laboured under foreign skies and foreign laws.

i18n.hi: कहानी शुरू होती है पंजाब से दूर, ठंडी पैसिफ़िक तटों पर, जहाँ भारतीय मज़दूर और छात्र पराए आसमान और पराए क़ानूनों के नीचे काम कर रहे थे।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a simple boarding house
panels.action: Inside a cramped wooden room lit by a single bulb, Kartar Singh Sarabha, slight and youthful, listens intently as older migrants argue about racism and empire, maps and newspapers spread on a rough table.

dialogue.text: Among them was Kartar Singh Sarabha, barely out of school, drifting between studies and work, absorbing every story of insult, exclusion and the long reach of British rule.

i18n.hi: उन्हीं में था कर्तार सिंह सराभा, मुश्किल से स्कूल से निकला, पढ़ाई और नौकरी के बीच भटकता, हर अपमान, हर बहिष्कार, हर अंग्रेज़ी ज़ुल्म की कहानी सोखता हुआ।

panels.shot: slow push-in on a crowded meeting hall interior
panels.action: In a modest hall with bare walls, migrants sit packed on benches; a makeshift dais holds speakers gesturing passionately while Kartar, seated near the front, leans forward, eyes burning.

dialogue.text: In 1913, these men and women formed the Hindustan Association of the Pacific Coast, a society of workers, exiles and students, and they chose a bold name for their paper—Ghadar, rebellion.

i18n.hi: 1913 में, इन्हीं औरतों-मर्दों ने पैसिफ़िक तट हिंदुस्तान एसोसिएशन बनाई—मज़दूरों, जफ़ाकशों, छात्रों की सोसायटी—और अपने अख़बार का नाम रखा बेख़ौफ़: ग़दर, बग़ावत।

panels.shot: over-the-shoulder close shot at the press
panels.action: Kartar operates a hand press in a cramped San Francisco printshop, sleeves rolled, ink on his fingers, as sheets bearing bold Gurmukhi and English headlines spill onto a table.

dialogue.text: On 1 November 1913, the first issue of Ghadar rolled off this press, printed in the languages of the migrants, with Kartar working not as a reader alone, but as a printer and organiser.

i18n.hi: 1 नवंबर 1913 को, ग़दर का पहला अंक इसी प्रेस से निकला, परदेसियों की ज़बानों में छपा, और कर्तार सिर्फ़ पाठक नहीं, प्रिंटर और संगठनकर्ता बनकर काम कर रहा था।

panels.shot: montage-style wide shot with layered vignettes
panels.action: A visual montage: bundles of Ghadar papers tied with twine; Kartar addressing a small group of workers; another vignette shows the newspaper in Urdu, Gurmukhi and English being packed into trunks and mailbags.

dialogue.text: Ghadar was not a local newsletter. It was printed in multiple scripts, mailed and hand-carried to mills, lumber camps, farms and bunkhouses across America, Canada, Asia and back toward India.

i18n.hi: ग़दर कोई मोहल्ला-पत्र नहीं था। ये कई लिपियों में छपता, डाक और हाथों से कारख़ानों, लकड़ी कैंपों, खेतों और मज़दूर बैरकों तक फैलता—अमेरिका, कनाडा, एशिया और वापस हिंदुस्तान की ओर।

panels.shot: wide shot of a ship deck at sea
panels.action: On the open deck of an ocean liner, Indian passengers huddle against the wind; one man discreetly passes a folded Ghadar issue to another as the vast Pacific stretches around them.

dialogue.text: Copies bore no royal portraits, no official seals. They carried poems, articles and calls to arms, urging soldiers and peasants to turn a distant war into a chance for liberation.

i18n.hi: इन प्रतियों पर न बादशाह की तस्वीर थी, न सरकारी मुहरें। इनमें कविताएँ, लेख और बग़ावत के बुलावे थे, जो सिपाहियों और किसानों को दूर की जंग को आज़ादी का मौक़ा बनाने को उकसाते थे।

panels.shot: medium shot in a Vancouver or Pacific Northwest camp
panels.action: In a rough timber camp, under a canvas awning, Kartar stands on a wooden crate addressing tired Sikh, Hindu and Muslim workers who clutch Ghadar sheets, their faces lined by work and weather.

dialogue.speaker: kartar_singh_sarabha
dialogue.text: These papers are our weapons. If we cannot carry rifles, we will carry words.

i18n.hi: ये काग़ज़ हमारे हथियार हैं। अगर बंदूक नहीं उठा सकते, तो शब्द उठाएँगे।

panels.shot: tight shot on a British official’s desk with layered documents
panels.action: A polished desk in a colonial office is cluttered with intercepted Ghadar issues, translated excerpts, and a confidential report stamped by the India Office, a British officer’s hand resting on the stack.

dialogue.text: British intelligence began to collect these issues, translating, annotating, and filing them as seditious documents, even as more copies slipped past their surveillance into villages and cantonments.

i18n.hi: ब्रिटिश ख़ुफ़िया ने इन अंकों को जमा करना शुरू किया—तरजमे, नोट्स, फाइलें—सबको राजद्रोही दस्तावेज़ ठहराया, जबकि और प्रतियाँ उनकी नज़रें चकमा देकर गाँवों और छावनियों तक पहुँचती रहीं।

panels.shot: wide shot of Europe-focused war map in an office
panels.action: A wall map showing Europe and Asia is marked with lines from India to Britain and Germany; a hand draws arrows from North America back to India as another marks the outbreak of war in 1914.

dialogue.text: In August 1914, the First World War began. Ghadar leaders read the news and saw opportunity: an empire at war abroad might be vulnerable at home.

i18n.hi: अगस्त 1914 में पहली विश्वयुद्ध छिड़ी। ग़दर के नेताओं ने ख़बर पढ़ी और मौक़ा देखा: बाहर जंग में फँसा सम्राज्य, घर में कमज़ोर हो सकता है।

panels.shot: medium shot in the San Francisco Ghadar office
panels.action: Inside the Ghadar office, walls lined with maps and portraits of earlier rebels, Kartar and comrades bend over letters and telegraphs, the young man pointing to Punjab on a map with determined intensity.

dialogue.text: Kartar joined in planning a return to India. Letters and emissaries moved along migrant routes, promising that soldiers and peasants would rise when the call came.

i18n.hi: कर्तार ने हिंदुस्तान लौटने की साज़िश में हाथ मिला दिया। ख़त और दूत, प्रवासी रास्तों पर दौड़े, वादा लेकर कि वक़्त पर सिपाही और किसान उठ खड़े होंगे।

panels.shot: wide shot on the deck of a homebound steamer
panels.action: Kartar stands at the rail of a crowded steamer heading west across the Pacific, a small bundle at his feet and a Ghadar issue folded in his hands, eyes fixed on the horizon.

dialogue.text: He sailed back as a teenager turned conspirator, carrying not only memories but names, contacts and the threads of a global network stitched together through print.

i18n.hi: वो लौटा तो किशोर नहीं, साज़िशी नौजवान बनकर—साथ में यादें ही नहीं, नाम, रिश्ते और प्रिंट से बुना हुआ एक आलमी जाल लेकर।

panels.shot: medium shot in a Punjab village courtyard
panels.action: In a Punjab village courtyard, Kartar meets returned migrants and local sympathisers; they huddle in the dusk as he unrolls a Ghadar issue and gestures toward nearby cantonments.

dialogue.text: Back in Punjab, he moved between villages, cantonment towns and railway lines, using Ghadar articles and songs to explain a plan that linked their fields to a war they could not see.

i18n.hi: पंजाब लौटकर, वो गाँवों, छावनी कस्बों और रेलवे लाइनों के बीच घूमता, ग़दर के लेख और गीतों से समझाता कि कैसे उनके खेत एक अनदेखी जंग से जुड़ते हैं।

panels.shot: tight shot on a hand passing coins and a note in a bazaar
panels.action: In a bustling bazaar, one man discreetly passes coins and a folded note to another near a stack of grain sacks, their eyes carefully avoiding each other.

dialogue.text: Money and messages moved in the same way the paper had moved—through workers, traders, ex-soldiers, each contact a risk, each conversation watched by informers and police.

i18n.hi: पैसा और पैग़ाम उसी रास्ते चले, जिस रास्ते अख़बार चला था—मज़दूरों, व्यापारियों, पूर्व-सिपाहियों के ज़रिए; हर रिश्ता ख़तरा, हर बात चीत पर मुख़बिर और पुलिस की नज़र।

panels.shot: medium shot in a colonial police station
panels.action: Inside a stark police room, a nervous man sits across from a British officer and an Indian sub-inspector, speaking hesitantly as a clerk writes, a bundle of Ghadar issues lying on the table.

dialogue.text: The sources we have—police reports, Home Department files, court testimonies—were written largely by enemies and informers, tracing meetings, rumours and plans with their own suspicions and limits.

i18n.hi: जो सबूत हमारे पास हैं—पुलिस रिपोर्टें, होम डिपार्टमेंट की फाइलें, अदालती बयान—ज़्यादातर दुश्मनों और मुख़बिरों ने लिखे, जो बैठकों, अफ़वाहों और योजनाओं को अपनी शक्की नज़र से दर्ज करते रहे।

panels.shot: dramatic medium shot of an arrest in an urban street
panels.action: On a Lahore street outside a printing or lodging house, plainclothes Indian policemen close in on Kartar; he stands straight, hands ready to be bound, his face calm but resolute.

dialogue.text: Before any uprising could spread, the conspiracy was penetrated. Arrests followed, and Kartar, with many others, was taken into custody to face charges in Lahore.

i18n.hi: किसी बग़ावत के फैलने से पहले ही, साज़िश में सेंध लग गई। गिरफ़्तारियाँ शुरू हुईं, और कर्तार कई साथियों के साथ पकड़ा गया, लाहौर में मुक़दमे के लिए।

panels.shot: wide interior shot of the Lahore conspiracy trial courtroom
panels.action: In the packed Lahore court, British judges sit elevated as Kartar and fellow accused stand in the dock, flanked by guards; bound volumes of the case and Ghadar issues lie on a table below.

dialogue.text: The Lahore Conspiracy Case gathered their actions into a single narrative of treason, with Ghadar issues produced as exhibits, cited as proof that words printed abroad had become offences at home.

i18n.hi: लाहौर षड्यंत्र केस ने उनकी हर हरकत को ग़द्दारी की एक कहानी बना दिया, ग़दर के अंक सबूत बनकर अदालत में रखे गए—दिखाने कि परदेस में छपे शब्द, मुल्क में जुर्म बन चुके हैं।

panels.shot: medium close-up of Kartar in the dock
panels.action: A close view of Kartar in the dock, shoulders squared, looking toward the bench, other accused faintly visible behind him, the dim courtroom light catching his youthful features.

dialogue.speaker: kartar_singh_sarabha
dialogue.text: If our printing is a crime, then my life is the price I offer.

i18n.hi: अगर हमारी छपाई जुर्म है, तो इसकी क़ीमत मेरी जान है।

panels.shot: somber medium shot in Lahore Central Jail yard
panels.action: Within high brick walls of Lahore jail at dawn, Kartar stands between guards in the yard, his hands loosely bound, looking up at the pale sky, the gallows structure stark in the background.

dialogue.text: On 16 November 1915, following the judgment of the Lahore Conspiracy Case, the nineteen-year-old Kartar Singh Sarabha was hanged, his role in Ghadar entered into the record as a capital crime.

i18n.hi: 16 नवंबर 1915 को, लाहौर षड्यंत्र केस के फ़ैसले के बाद, उन्नीस साल के कर्तार सिंह सराभा को फाँसी दी गई—ग़दर में उसका रोल क़ानूनी रेकॉर्ड में एक फाँसी-लायक जुर्म बनकर दर्ज हुआ।

panels.shot: wide composite shot showing archives and later readers
panels.action: A composite scene: on one side, colonial archival shelves hold bound Home Department files and preserved Ghadar issues; on the other, decades later, scholars and activists sit in a reading room studying the same documents.

dialogue.text: Later historians, reading these hostile files alongside surviving issues of Ghadar, traced not only a failed plot, but a transnational network of workers, students and exiles who turned print into a bridge for rebellion.

i18n.hi: बाद के इतिहासकारों ने, इन दुश्मन फाइलों को ग़दर के बचे अंकों के साथ पढ़कर, सिर्फ़ नाकाम साज़िश नहीं, बल्कि मज़दूरों, छात्रों और जफ़ाकशों का एक सरहदी जाल देखा, जिसने छपाई को बग़ावत का पुल बना दिया।

panels.shot: poetic wide shot dissolving between San Francisco press and Punjab fields
panels.action: A split image blends the old San Francisco printshop where Kartar once worked the press with distant Punjab fields at dusk, Ghadar sheets drifting like leaves between the two landscapes.

dialogue.text: Kartar Singh Sarabha’s brief life shows how a hand press in San Francisco could shake courtrooms in Lahore, and how words carried by migrants can turn borders, ships and fields into a single contested ground.

i18n.hi: कर्तार सिंह सराभा की छोटी-सी ज़िंदगी दिखाती है कि सैन फ़्रांसिस्को की छोटी प्रेस कैसे लाहौर की अदालतें हिला सकती है, और कैसे प्रवासियों के कंधों पर चले शब्द, सरहदों, जहाज़ों और खेतों को एक ही जंग का मैदान बना सकते हैं।

subtitle_i18n.en: A teenage printer, a Pacific press, and a conspiracy carried in newsprint
subtitle_i18n.hi: एक नौजवान प्रिंटर, पैसिफ़िक की प्रेस, और ख़बरों में छपा षड्यंत्र
